meta.notes: Physical constants hard-coded in JS; this file is data-only.

sun.name: Sun
sun.note: Central reference body for heliocentric elements; placed at origin with no heliocentric orbit. Axial tilt is Sun’s obliquity to the ecliptic at J2000.

bodies.name: Moon
bodies.note: Angles Ω, ω, and M at J2000 available from JPL HORIZONS/SSD; most fact sheets list a, e, i and period only.

bodies.name: Phobos
bodies.note: Angles to be taken from JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements (J2000).

bodies.name: Deimos
bodies.note: Angles to be taken from JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements (J2000).

bodies.name: Amalthea
bodies.note: Angles L0, Ω, ϖ at J2000 available from JPL SSD; derive M=L0−ϖ and ω=ϖ−Ω.

bodies.name: Io
bodies.note: JPL SSD mean elements at J2000 provide Ω≈43.977°, ϖ≈128.106° (ω≈84.129°), L0≈171.016°; compute M=L0−ϖ. Use official table.

bodies.name: Europa
bodies.note: Use JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements (J2000) for Ω, ω, M.

bodies.name: Ganymede
bodies.note: Use JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements (J2000) for Ω, ω, M.

bodies.name: Callisto
bodies.note: Use JPL SSD Planetary Satellite Mean Elements (J2000) for Ω, ω, M.

bodies.name: Mimas
bodies.note: Angles available from JPL SSD mean elements (J2000).

bodies.note: Angles available from JPL SSD mean elements (J2000).

bodies.name: Triton
bodies.note: Retrograde orbit. Use JPL SSD mean elements (J2000) for Ω, ω, and mean longitude to compute M.

bodies.name: Prometheus
bodies.note: Basic orbital parameters from IMCCE (equator frame). J2000 mean angles (Ω, ω, M) should be taken from JPL SSD mean-elements.

bodies.name: Pan
bodies.note: Pan’s mean elements are from Spitale et al. (2006) Table 4 at epoch J2000 (JED 2451545.0). ω and M computed as ω=ϖ−Ω and M=λ−ϖ.

bodies.name: Atlas
bodies.note: IMCCE provides a, e, i and period relative to Saturn’s equator; J2000 mean angles (Ω, ω, M) are available in JPL SSD mean-elements tables but not accessible here.

bodies.name: Pandora
bodies.note: Basic orbital parameters from IMCCE (equator frame). J2000 mean angles (Ω, ω, M) should be taken from JPL SSD mean-elements.

bodies.name: Janus
bodies.note: Basic orbital parameters from IMCCE (equator frame). J2000 mean angles (Ω, ω, M) should be taken from JPL SSD mean-elements.

bodies.name: Epimetheus
bodies.note: Basic orbital parameters from IMCCE (equator frame). J2000 mean angles (Ω, ω, M) should be taken from JPL SSD mean-elements.

bodies.name: Puck
bodies.note: Period from Veiga et al. (2006 A&A 454, 683) and widely cited catalogs (~0.769 d). Precise J2000 mean-element angles are tabulated by JPL SSD but not accessible here.

bodies.name: Proteus
bodies.note: Mean radius and basic orbit from NASA factsheets/JPL; detailed J2000 mean angles appear in JPL SSD mean-elements and Jacobson (2009).

bodies.name: Nereid
bodies.note: Elements (a,e,i,period) consistent with ICRF/J2000 reference and literature (e.g., Iorio 2010 using JPL Horizons/SSD). J2000 mean-element angles (Ω, ω, M) should be taken from JPL SSD mean-elements.

bodies.name: Ceres
bodies.note: M_deg computed at J2000 (TT) using SBDB period and Tp; other angles are SBDB J2000-referenced osculating elements.

bodies.name: Haumea
bodies.note: Estimated M at J2000 (TT) from M = n*(t−Tp) mod 360 using n = 0.00350520 deg/day and Tp = JD 2500289.4542 (2133-06-16).

bodies.name: Makemake
bodies.note: M_deg evaluated at J2000 (TT) from SBDB period and pericenter time; other angles are SBDB J2000-referenced osculating elements.

bodies.name: Eris
bodies.note: Orbital elements are heliocentric osculating referenced to the IAU76/J2000 ecliptic at epoch 2025-05-05 (TDB) as provided by JPL SBDB; for strict J2000(TT) elements, query JPL HORIZONS.
